metadata.title: TMUA 2017 · Paper 1
metadata.description: Worked steps, progressive hints and reviewed follow-up questions.

matches.rationale: The same rational/radical simplification produces powers that can be integrated directly; checks the antiderivative coefficients.
Rewrites fractional and negative powers and integrates them. Definite bounds replace the original initial-value constant step.
Expands a rational square into powers before integrating, reinforcing the simplification-first route and careful signs.
Simplifies a quotient into fractional powers before differentiating; rehearses the power-rule route without quotient-rule overhead.
Simplifies a radical quotient into powers and differentiates, retaining the negative-power signs.
Simplifies and differentiates before substituting a numerical input, matching the original order of operations; it requires one derivative rather than two.
A perpendicular bisector is found from its gradient and point, then its axis intercept is located; the equal-distance route is also available.

The equal-radius intersection line is a perpendicular bisector of the centres, so it can be constructed using the same negative reciprocal gradient and point-gradient equation. Circle equidistance is additional work, and there is no area or axis-intercept task in the follow-up: prerequisite transfer only.
Constructs a normal using the negative reciprocal gradient, finds both axis intercepts and measures their separation.
Given factors become evaluations at two specified roots; the remainder theorem is used with remainder zero.
A linear factor determines the unknown coefficient by one substitution before polynomial factorisation.
Uses the remainder theorem as a polynomial identity deduction; isolates why substituting the divisor’s root determines the remainder.

Both determine strict polynomial sign sets and intersect the component restrictions. The 2017 task additionally constructs a single quadratic inequality representing that overlap; the 2020 task asks for the interval directly.

Both solve factor-sign inequalities on intervals. The cubic task isolates sign-chart construction; the 2017 task additionally intersects a second restriction and encodes the overlap as a single quadratic inequality.

Both use radii perpendicular to a tangent to construct right triangles and infer a slope-related quantity. The candidate recovers the tangent of an angle; the original recovers the tangent line’s axis intercept.
Builds centre-distance equations for internal and external tangency, reinforcing the need to select the correct geometric configuration. It does not repeat the tangent intercept construction.

This transfer practises retaining circle radii while modelling a geometric distance with Pythagoras. The follow-up obtains centre separation from coordinates and then a boundary gap; it does not reproduce the original tangent or similar-triangle steps.
Nonconsecutive AP terms coincide with consecutive GP terms; eliminate the AP difference before using the ratio and sum.
A GP whose selected terms form an AP gives a polynomial in the ratio and requires choosing the convergent branch.
Combines AP and GP expressions and eliminates the arithmetic difference to use the sum information.
Directly repeats the trigonometric product sign-chart method, with different sine/cosine factors and intervals.
Reduces radicals to signed trigonometric products, locates the allowed quadrants and counts their inclusive endpoints.
Exposes a lost sign branch in a tangent-positive argument; reinforces retaining every original sign condition instead of taking an unjustified positive square root.
Uses the same equilateral-triangle area calculation, then counts triangular ends and rectangular sides of a prism.
Isolates the prerequisite of completing squares in a circle equation and reading radius squared, including the leading coefficient.
sharedKnowledge: Complete squares in a circle equation

matches.rationale: Both calculate triangle areas from circle radii and exact central angles. The original totals equilateral triangles in a regular hexagon; the candidate uses the sine-area formula to recover a central angle, then adds chord and maximum-altitude work. This is an explicit triangle-area prerequisite transfer.
sharedKnowledge: Triangle area from two radii and an included angle
Decompose an inscribed circle figure into triangles

matches.rationale: Differentiation at a fixed x-value produces a parameter quadratic whose minimum is found by completing the square.
A positive denominator’s quadratic minimum determines a reciprocal maximum; the hidden variable is an exponential rather than the original parameter.

This transfer practises completing the square and checking that an extremum is attained on the permitted input range. The original minimises a quadratic denominator to maximise a normal gradient; the follow-up maximises a quadratic over a bounded sine-generated range and uses no differentiation or reciprocal.
sharedKnowledge: quadratic extrema on an allowed range

matches.rationale: A recurrence produces a repeated block; prove the repetition and group the large-index sum into complete blocks.
A trigonometric sequence has a six-term cycle. It rehearses modular position and full-cycle sums rather than a rational recurrence.
Groups a long trigonometric sum into four-term periodic blocks; directly practises handling the remainder after complete cycles.
Input reflection transforms the integration interval, while signed and unsigned areas must be distinguished.
Uses additivity of overlapping signed integrals to recover component areas, reinforcing what an integral over a specific interval represents.
Combines integrals on adjacent intervals into one zero integral; targets signed accumulation and correct boundaries rather than input translation.
Equates selected coefficients from two expansions and carefully keeps the different powers of the nonzero parameter.
Identifies a binomial degree from term positions, then forms a ratio of specified coefficients.
Finds two selected coefficients through nested power choices and imposes the given relationship on the parameter.
Different bases become powers of one common base, producing ordinary simultaneous relations in the exponents.
Logarithmic substitutions turn simultaneous equations into manageable algebra before recovering original values.
Undoing logarithms turns a simultaneous system into algebra; original domain checks select valid solutions.
Both track the trapezium error when a graph is transformed, rather than recalculating all strips.
Both preserve quadrature error under reflection and reverse it under a vertical complement.

Prerequisite transfer: compare the position of a chord with a curve and distinguish bending from the sign of its height or gradient. The original uses that geometry after transformations to classify trapezium error; the candidate establishes the necessary second-derivative sign from all midpoint chords.
sharedKnowledge: separate curvature from height and gradient

matches.rationale: Factors a fractional-power derivative, removes its positive factor, and finds the exact interval of decrease.

Prerequisite transfer: compute a derivative and check its sign independently of the sign of the function. The candidate then tests an all-real derivative premise and one height failure; it does not repeat the original derivative-interval calculation.
Builds a derivative sign chart to determine monotonic intervals and turning heights before counting roots.
A quadratic threshold is located between adjacent integers, with the strict inequality deciding the first permitted integer.
An arithmetic-sum inequality is translated into an algebraic condition and tested without assuming individual term signs.
A geometric-series sum has both a convergence condition and a strict threshold; extends careful domain and boundary checking to a different sum formula.
Uses log laws to recognise a straight line in transformed axes, distinguishing power and exponential relationships.
sharedKnowledge: Multiplicative quantities as additive log terms

matches.rationale: Names a nested logarithmic quantity to compare two straight lines; it reinforces transforming the whole input correctly rather than repeating horizontal log scaling.
Uses Vieta’s relations to recover a new symmetric root expression without solving the roots individually.
sharedKnowledge: Construct a polynomial from symmetric root data

matches.rationale: Reconstructs a quadratic from symmetric information about two unknown quantities, practising the sum/product algebra.
sharedKnowledge: reverse order under a negative scale

matches.rationale: Tracks how strict negative orderings change under multiplication and division; targets the crucial reversal when scaling roots by a negative constant.
sharedKnowledge: reverse order under a negative scale

matches.rationale: Uses side positivity and an altitude to derive strict triangle-existence inequalities. It directly rehearses the feasibility step, but uses sine/SSA rather than the cosine rule.
Checks acute and obtuse angle branches against the triangle angle sum. It targets valid angle ranges and rejecting degenerate/impossible configurations, not the original side formula.

review.method: Exact question crops and answer letters; compare demanded knowledge steps with official worked solutions. Every follow-up is from another year or the early specimen.

coverageNotes.note: Three further cosine-rule/triangle-feasibility bound problems were not identified in the official archive. Follow-ups are labelled targeted transfers in side feasibility, angle feasibility, and cancellation before trigonometric range bounds. Do not describe them as exact cosine-rule analogues.
Official answer uses non-strict derivative endpoint conventions. Teaching identifies zero-derivative boundaries explicitly rather than calling them strictly increasing/decreasing signs.
